subject: general
question: What was the theme for National Safety Day, observed on 4 March 2025?

options.text: Safety & Well-being Crucial for Viksit Bharat

solution:
The correct answer is __**Safety & Well-being Crucial for Viksit Bharat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The theme for National Safety Day 2025, observed on **4th March 2025**, was "Safety & Well-being Crucial for Viksit Bharat."
 
• The theme emphasizes the importance of safety and well-being as foundational pillars for building a developed and prosperous India.
 
• National Safety Day is organized annually by the **National Safety Council (NSC)** of India, established in 1966 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
 
• The day aims to raise awareness regarding workplace safety, road safety, and environmental protection among the Indian public.
 
• It serves as a platform to engage industries, organizations, and individuals in adopting best practices for safety and health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Safety Council (NSC)**

 
 
• The National Safety Council was established in 1966 as a non-profit, autonomous body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
 
• The council works to promote voluntary compliance with safety, health, and environmental standards in industries.
 
• It provides training, consultancy, and resources to enhance workplace safety and health.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of National Safety Day**
 
 
• The day focuses on creating awareness about safety measures for reducing accidents and injuries across different sectors.
 
• It encourages organizations to adopt robust safety systems and inculcate a safety-first culture among employees.
 
 
 
• **Workplace Safety in India**
 
 
• Industries such as construction, manufacturing, and chemicals are particularly vulnerable to workplace accidents.
 
• Regulations like the Factories Act, 1948, and the Occupational Safety, Health, and Working Conditions Code, 2020, play a key role in ensuring safety standards.
 
 
 
• **Road Safety in India**
 
 
• India ranks among the highest in the world for road accidents, with over 1.5 lakh fatalities annually.
 
• Initiatives like the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, aim to reduce accidents by implementing stricter penalties and enforcement measures.
